items.title: Butch Miles interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, October 9, 2020 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: I’ve only heard in my entire life two people that would say something that was outrageous and then back it up completely. And those two people were Buddy Rich and Muhammad Ali.

ctx.x: Well it sounds like you were lucky to, playing with Basie and those folks. You’ve got life lessons from them. And now, our generation is the one that’s, it’s our turn to pass them on I guess you could say.

It is. You’re absolutely right about that. I learned so much, and I did so much growing up on that bus and those one-nighters, and those stages and gig after gig after gig and meeting people, myriads of different folks from all walks of life who either loved the music or hated the music. It was okay because it was just the experience. I did an awful lot of growing up and that was my experience with the band. And I’m still growing. I find myself now thinking about things I did 30 years ago and I realize I could…
I took note of, in your first interview you said a wonderful thing about Al Grey, because on the bandstand, especially when you first joined he would like Basie’s playing an intro
